generations.prompt:
Two pictures come with this request.

IMAGE 1 is the picture you edit: the lower part of a frame of our own rhythm game's play screen. Dark note lanes run away from the camera, a glowing red judge line crosses them, under it lies a strip of eight thin dark slots with slanted ends (outlined in grey) over a red hairline, and under that, between the two thin side rails (hairlines with small ticks), lies the gear's lower panel: a wide slab that runs down to the bottom edge of the image, widening toward the camera. In image 1 the panel is a FLAT LAYOUT DRAWING OF AN LED DOT-MATRIX DISPLAY: a regular grid of small round dots, 128 across and 55 deep, on black. Most dots are unlit (faint dark dots). The lit ones draw black-and-red graphics: three broad slanting bands of dim red dots; orbit lines one dot wide in bright red (two large slanted ovals, a small flat loop at the right, a ring at the left); at each side a block of bright red dots and a bar of white dots that overlap; at the upper left a small diamond of red dots and a few single grey-white dots; near the bottom at each side a cluster of eight round blobs of bright red dots in two rows; at the near edge three slanting stripes of white dots at the left and three narrower red ones right of the middle; three red chevrons and two small marks of white dots at the right; a small ring of white dots at the bottom middle; and two upright lines of grey-white dots, one near each side. The middle of the panel is empty (unlit dots and the dim bands only). The drawing shows exactly which dots are lit and in which colour.

IMAGE 2 is the DESIGN REFERENCE for the colours and the mood only: a small concept picture of this panel (enlarged, blurry): black with glowing red and a little white, dark and tense. Its graphics are smooth; here everything is shown by LED dots instead. Its lettering and numbers (SCORE, COMBO) are NOT wanted: write no text at all.

Keep image 1's framing EXACTLY: the same camera, the same zoom, the same crop; your picture must overlay image 1 pixel for pixel, so the judge line, the strip of slots, the red hairline and the two side rails stay at exactly the same places and sizes. Do not zoom in, do not crop, do not widen, do not recompose, do not enlarge or shrink the panel. Repaint ONLY the panel: the area under the red hairline, between the inner edges of the two side rails, down to the bottom edge of the image. Keep every other pixel exactly as it is: the lanes, the notes, the judge line and its glow, the strip of slots, the red hairline, the rails, the dark background.

The panel becomes that LED DOT-MATRIX DISPLAY BOARD as a real thing (like a stadium scoreboard or an LED sign lying flat), as a photorealistic 3D render at the finish of a commercial console game, seen exactly from this camera: a matte black board carrying a perfectly regular grid of small round LEDs, exactly the grid of dots drawn, foreshortened by the camera exactly as in image 1 (the rows of dots get smaller and closer toward the far edge and stay parallel to the judge line).

1. EVERY DOT OF THE DRAWING IS ONE LED: it stays at its place in the grid and keeps its colour and its brightness: bright red, dim red (the broad bands: LEDs glowing at low power), white, grey-white, or unlit. Do not move, add or remove dots, do not change which dots are lit, and do not merge the dots into solid shapes or smooth lines: everything is made of separate round dots with black board between them.

2. THE LIT LEDS: each is a tiny round lens glowing from inside, brightest at its centre, with a small soft halo. Where many are lit together (the blocks, the bars, the blobs of the clusters, the stripes) their light lays a faint glow of their colour on the black board between and round them. The bright red is saturated and intense; the dim red of the bands is a deep, quiet wine red; the white is clean and bright.

3. THE UNLIT LEDS: tiny dark, glassy lenses in the black board, barely seen, each with a pin-point reflection, so that the regular grid shows faintly everywhere, also in the empty middle.

4. THE BOARD: matte black, flat and clean, with no frame, no seams and no screws.

Dark, sharp and precise.

Everything stays inside the rails; nothing rises over the rails or above the strip of slots, and the panel runs on down past the bottom edge of the image (no front edge is seen). Nothing else is on the panel: no screens, no number boxes, no cards, no buttons, no knobs, no cables, no people, no hands.

No text, letters or numbers anywhere, no logos, no watermark, and nothing over the lanes. Colours: black; red (close to #F61222) and a dark wine red (close to #3A060B); white.
